source.title: The Lyapin's Notebook: A Collection of Unsolved Problems in Semigroup Theory

accepted.question_text: Given a semigroup S and a system of equations with constants from S, characterize those types of equations or systems for which there is an algorithm deciding, for every assignment of the constants, whether the system is solvable in some finite extension of S.

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1. (S. Kublanovsky, M. Sapir) Describe the types of equations or systems of equations for which there exists an algorithm that decides for any values of the constants whether the given system is solvable in some finite extension of the original semigroup.

accepted.question_text: Describe exactly which semigroups occur as divisors, that is, homomorphic images of subsemigroups, of (i) finite Brandt semigroups and (ii) finite 0-simple semigroups given in Rees matrix form by a sandwich matrix whose entries are only 0 and 1.
Determine whether there is an algorithm that, given a finite semigroup, decides whether it can be embedded into the power semigroup of some finite group, equivalently of some periodic group.

evidence.quote: Problem 1.3. (S. Bershadsky, S. Kublanovsky) Is there an algorithm that decides whether a given finite semigroup is embeddable into a power semigroup over some finite group (periodic group) (see Chapter 5 of this notebook)?

accepted.question_text: For the full transformation semigroup T(n), consisting of all self-maps of an n-element set under composition, determine a complete description of the semigroup identities that hold in T(n).

evidence.quote: Problem 2.1. (E.S. Lyapin) Describe the identities of the full transformation semigroup T(n) on an n-element set.

accepted.question_text: Classify semigroup varieties that are locally residually finite for the standard predicates studied in this area, meaning that every finitely generated semigroup in the variety satisfies the corresponding residual-finiteness property.

evidence.quote: Problem 2.2. (S. Kublanovsky) Describe locally residually finite varieties of semigroups for known predicates.

accepted.question_text: Fix n and let RS_n be the variety generated by all 0-simple semigroups satisfying the identity x^2 = x^{n+2}. Describe the covers of RS_n both inside the lattice of all semigroup varieties and inside the sublattice of varieties satisfying x^2 = x^{n+2}.

evidence.quote:
Let RSn denote the variety generated by all 0-simple semigroups satisfying the identity x
2 = x
n+2. Such varieties and their subvarieties are called Rees-Sushkevich varieties (see [14]).
Problem 2.3. (S. Kublanovsky) Describe the covers of the semigroup variety RSn in the lattice
of varieties of all semigroups and in the lattice of varieties satisfying the identity x
2 = x
n+2
.

accepted.question_text: Classify the periodic semigroup varieties that are generated by regular semigroups.
accepted.context_brief: periodic varieties generated by regular semigroups

evidence.quote: Problem 2.4. (S. Kublanovsky) Describe periodic varieties generated by regular semigroups.

accepted.question_text: Let u be a non-blocking word with c(u) distinct letters, where m(u) is the smallest alphabet size for which there exists an infinite word avoiding all substitution instances of u. Determine m(u) in terms of u.

evidence.quote:
Problem 2.5. (I. Melnichuk) Let c(u) denote the number of distinct letters occuring in the word
u. Let m(u) denote the minimal number of letters in a finite alphabet A for which there exists an
infinite word over A that does not contain images of u under substitutions. Determine the number
m(u) for a non-blocking word u containing c(u) letters.

accepted.question_text: Decide whether the class of finite completely 0-simple semigroups over Abelian groups that have a finite identity basis is recursive, in particular whether this is true for those over the two-element group.
accepted.context_brief: finite basis problem for completely 0-simple semigroups

evidence.quote:
Problem 2.6. (G. Mashevitzky) Is the set of finite finitely based completely 0-simple semigroups
over Abelian groups, in particular, over a two-element group, recursive?

accepted.question_text: Determine when a system of identical inequalities, also called identical relations of precedence, defines exactly the same class of ordered semigroups as some system of identities.
accepted.context_brief: inequalities versus identities in ordered semigroups

evidence.quote:
Problem 2.7. (E.S. Lyapin) Under what conditions is a system of identical inequalities (identical
relations of precedence) equivalent to a system of identities?

accepted.question_text: Classify the varieties of ordered semigroups that possess covers in the lattice of varieties of ordered semigroups.

evidence.quote:
Problem 2.8. (E.S. Lyapin) Describe all varieties of ordered semigroups that have covers in the
lattice of varieties of ordered semigroups.

accepted.question_text: Classify the varieties of ordered semigroups for which every semigroup in the variety admits only the trivial compatible partial order.
accepted.context_brief: ordered varieties with only trivial orders

evidence.quote:
Problem 2.9. (V. Makaridina) Describe all varieties of ordered semigroups in which every semi
group has only the trivial order.

accepted.question_text: Classify the semigroup varieties whose endomorphic function is unbounded, that is, the endomorphic varieties of semigroups.

evidence.quote: Problem 3.1. (S. Kublanovsky) Describe endomorphic varieties of semigroups.

accepted.question_text: Is every variety of commutative semigroups characterized by an endomorphic function that is identical, rather than merely unbounded?
accepted.context_brief: commutative varieties and identical endomorphic functions

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.2. (S. Kublanovsky) Is it true that for every variety of commutative semigroups its
endomorphic function is identical?

accepted.question_text: Is it true that every endomorphic variety of semigroups has an endomorphic function that is identical?

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.3. (S. Kublanovsky) Is it true that for any endomorphic variety of semigroups its
endomorphic function is identical?

accepted.question_text: Obtain quantitative estimates for the endomorphic function for the principal basic classes of semigroups.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.4. (S. Kublanovsky) Obtain estimates for the values of the endomorphic function for
various basic classes of semigroups.

accepted.question_text: Classify finitely generated Lesokhin semigroups without idempotents, where a commutative semigroup is called a Lesokhin semigroup if every endomorphism is a power map sending each element to a fixed power of itself.

evidence.quote:

tents.

accepted.question_text: Classify commutative semigroups whose every endomorphism is injective.

evidence.quote:

injective.

accepted.question_text: Classify finitely generated commutative separative E-semigroups, where an E-semigroup is a commutative semigroup isomorphic, under pointwise multiplication, to the semigroup of all its endomorphisms.

evidence.quote:
A commutative semigroup is called an E-semigroup if it is isomorphic to the semigroup
of all its endomorphisms under pointwise multiplication.
...
Problem 3.7. (A.A. Borisov) Describe finitely generated commutative separative E-semigroups.

accepted.question_text: Classify commutative semigroups whose endomorphism semigroup, under pointwise multiplication, is cancellative.

evidence.quote:

phisms (with pointwise multiplication) is cancelative.

accepted.question_text: Classify commutative semigroups whose endomorphism semigroup under pointwise multiplication is isomorphic either to the additive semigroup of all positive rational numbers or to the additive semigroup of all nonnegative rational numbers.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.9. (A.A. Borisov) Describe commutative semigroups whose semigroups of endomor
phisms (with pointwise multiplication) are isomorphic to one of the following semigroups:
(1) the additive semigroup of all positive rational numbers;
(2) the additive semigroup of all non negative rational numbers.

accepted.question_text: Classify commutative semigroups whose endomorphism semigroup under pointwise multiplication is a free semigroup.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.10. (A.A. Borisov) Describe commutative semigroups whose semigroups of endomor
phisms (with pointwise multiplication) are free semigroups.

accepted.question_text: For a semigroup without idempotents, define a < b when a = ab = ba, and define the chain rank to be the maximum length of a finite chain for this strict partial order, or infinite if arbitrarily long finite chains exist. Is the chain rank of every finitely generated, or even every finitely presented, semigroup without idempotents finite?

evidence.quote:
Let S be a semigroup without idempotents. For elements a, b ∈ S we write a < b if
a = ab = ba. It is easy to verify that < is a strict partial order on S. ...
Problem 3.11. (A.A. Borisov) Is it true that the chain rank of any finitely generated (or finitely
presented) semigroup without idempotents is finite?

accepted.question_text: Classify commutative semigroups that have exactly four endomorphisms.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.12. (A.A. Borisov) Describe commutative semigroups that have exactly four endo
morphisms.

accepted.question_text: For natural classes of mathematical structures, such as ordered sets and relatively free algebras, and for subsemigroups of their endomorphism semigroups, determine which subclasses of structures are determined up to isomorphism by those semigroups and which subsemigroups already suffice to determine the structures up to isomorphism.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.13. (E.S. Lyapin) For natural classes of mathematical structures - such as ordered
sets, relatively free algebras, and for subsemigroups of endomorphism semigroups of these structures
- determine:
(1) Subclasses of structures defined up to isomorphism by these semigroups;
(2) Subsemigroups of endomorphism semigroups that determine these structures up to isomor
phism.

accepted.question_text: Describe the endomorphism semigroup and the endomorphism or automorphism tower for endomorphism semigroups of semigroups free in basic semigroup classes, in particular idempotent, commutative Clifford, and Clifford semigroups, and also for endomorphism semigroups of algebras free in basic classes of mathematical structures.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.14. (G. Mashevitzky) Describe the endomorphism semigroup and the tower of endo
morphisms (automorphisms)
(1) for endomorphism semigroups of semigroups free in basic classes of semigroups, in partic
ular in the classes of idempotent, commutative Clifford, and Clifford semigroups;
(2) for endomorphism semigroups of algebras free in basic classes of mathematical structures.

accepted.question_text: Classify (i) transformation semigroups that are closed in the pointwise topology and (ii) endomorphism semigroups that are closed in a topology of Zariski type.

evidence.quote:
Problem 3.15. (G. Mashevitzky)
(1) Describe transformation semigroups that are closed in the pointwise topology.
(2) Describe endomorphism semigroups that are closed in a topology of Zarisky type.

accepted.question_text: Let C_0 be a class of finite 0-simple semigroups and let K be one of the Birkhoff operators HP, HPS, or SHPS. Is the class K(C_0) decidable?

evidence.quote:
Problem 4.1. (S.I. Kublanovsky) Let C0 be a class of finite 0-simple semigroups. Is the class
K(C0) decidable, where K is one of the operators HP, HPS, SHPS?

accepted.question_text: Determine whether the class of finite 0-simple semigroups over groups belonging to a pseudovariety of groups with decidable universal theory is completely solvable, and likewise whether the analogous class of finite Brandt semigroups with the same kind of restriction on maximal subgroups is completely solvable.

evidence.quote:
Problem 4.2. (S.I. Kublanovsky)
(1) Is the class of finite 0-simple semigroups over groups, belonging to a pseudovariety of groups
with decidable universal theory, completely solvable?
(2) The same question for the class of finite Brandt semigroups, under a similar restriction on
maximal subgroups.

accepted.question_text: Is the class of finite regular aperiodic semigroups completely solvable? Here a semigroup is aperiodic when all of its subgroups are trivial.
accepted.context_brief: complete solvability of regular aperiodic semigroups

evidence.quote:
Problem 4.3. (S.I. Kublanovsky) Is the class of finite regular aperiodic semigroups completely
solvable?
Recall that a semigroup is aperiodic if all its subgroups are trivial.

accepted.question_text: Determine whether (i) the class of finite regular orthodox semigroups is completely solvable and (ii) the class of finite regular semigroups whose idempotents lie in a fixed variety of idempotent semigroups is completely solvable.

evidence.quote:
Problem 4.4. (S.I. Kublanovsky)
(1) Is the class of finite regular orthodox semigroups completely solvable?
(2) The same question for the class of finite regular semigroups, whose idempotents belong to
a given variety of idempotent semigroups.

accepted.question_text: Let K be one of HP, HPS, SHP, or SHPS, and let Φ be an arbitrary finite class of finite semigroups. Is the kernel Cor(K(Φ)) = {M in K(Φ) | HSP(M) is contained in K(Φ)} decidable?
accepted.context_brief: decidability of kernels of generated classes

evidence.quote:
Problem 4.6. (S.I. Kublanovsky) Let K be one of the operators HP, HPS, SHP, SHPS, and let Φ
be an arbitrary finite class of finite semigroups. Is the class Cor(K(Φ)) decidable?

accepted.question_text: If two finite semigroups have isomorphic power semigroups, must the original finite semigroups themselves be isomorphic?

evidence.quote:
Problem 5.1. (E. M. Mogiljanskaja) Does the isomorphism of power semigroups implies the
isomorphism of the original semigroups in the class of finite semigroups?

accepted.question_text: Find necessary and sufficient conditions for a regular semigroup to embed into the power semigroup of a periodic group.
accepted.context_brief: regular semigroups in periodic power semigroups

evidence.quote:
Problem 5.2. (S.G. Bershadsky, S.I. Kublanovsky) Find necessary and sufficient conditions for
the embeddability of a regular semigroup into the power one over a periodic group.

accepted.question_text: Is every periodic commutative semigroup embeddable into the power semigroup of a periodic Abelian group?

evidence.quote:
Problem 5.3. (S.G. Bershadsky, S.I. Kublanovsky) Is every periodic commutative semigroup em
beddable into the power semigroup over a periodic Abelian group?

accepted.question_text: Suppose every finitely generated subsemigroup of a semigroup S embeds into the power semigroup of some periodic group. Must S itself embed into the power semigroup of a periodic group?

evidence.quote:
Problem 5.4. (S.G. Bershadsky, S.I. Kublanovsky) Is it true that if every finitely generated sub
semigroup of a semigroup S is embeddable into the power semigroup over some periodic group then
S is also embeddable into the power semigroup over a periodic group?

accepted.question_text: Find general necessary and sufficient, or at least broadly applicable, criteria for when a semigroup embeds into the power semigroup of a periodic group.

evidence.quote:
Problem 5.5. (S.G. Bershadsky, S.I. Kublanovsky) Find general embeddability criteria (necessary
and/or sufficient conditions) for a semigroup to be embeddable into the power semigroup over a
periodic group.

accepted.question_text: Find an analogue of Birkhoff's theorem for inclusive varieties of semigroups by determining a minimal family of Birkhoff-type closure operators that characterizes exactly when a class of semigroups is an inclusive variety.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.1. (G. Mashevitzky) Find a theorem for inclusive varieties analogous to the Birkhoff
theorem for varieties; that is, determine a (minimal) set of Birkhoff type operators such that a
class of semigroups forms an inclusive variety if and only if it is closed under these operators.

accepted.question_text: Classify inclusive varieties of semigroups whose lattices of inclusive subvarieties are finite or countable.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.2. (G. Mashevitzky) Determine all inclusive varieties with finite or countable lattices
of inclusive subvarieties.

accepted.question_text: Determine (i) minimal and maximal inclusive varieties of semigroups that cannot be defined by elementary identical inclusions, (ii) elementary inclusive varieties all of whose inclusive subvarieties are elementary, and (iii) nonelementary inclusive varieties of periodic semigroups whose inclusive supervarieties inside the class of periodic semigroups are also nonelementary.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.3. (G. Mashevitzky)
(1) Find minimal (maximal) inclusive varieties of semigroups that cannot be defined by ele
mentary identical inclusions.
(2) Describe elementary inclusive varieties of semigroups all of whose inclusive subvarieties
are elementary.
(3) Describe nonelementary inclusive varieties of periodic semigroups whose inclusive super
varieties in the class of periodic semigroups are nonelementary.

accepted.question_text: Classify semigroups from the standard basic classes up to inclusive equivalence, meaning equivalence with respect to satisfying the same identical inclusions.

evidence.quote:
We call two semigroups inclusively equivalent if they satisfy the same identical inclusions;
equivalently if they generate the same inclusive variety.
Problem 6.4. (G. Mashevitzky) Classify semigroups from the basic classes of semigroups up to
inclusive equivalence.

accepted.question_text: Determine which semigroups from the standard basic classes are uniquely determined up to isomorphism by the identical inclusions they satisfy.

evidence.quote:
A semigroup is said to be determined by identical inclusions up to isomorphism if every
semigroup satisfying the same identical inclusions is isomorphic to it.
Problem 6.5. (G. Mashevitzky) Find semigroups from the basic classes of semigroups determined
by their identical inclusions up to isomorphism.

accepted.question_text: Classify the ordinary semigroup varieties whose finitely generated free semigroups can be separated from one another by identical inclusions.
accepted.context_brief: free semigroups separated by identical inclusions

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.6. (G. Mashevitzky) Describe ordinary semigroup varieties such that their finitely
generated free semigroups can be separated from each other by identical inclusions.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.7. (G. Mashevitzky) Does there exist a nonelementary inclusive variety of idempotent
semigroups?

accepted.context_brief: finite members forming elementary inclusive varieties

accepted.context_brief: finite generators with infinite inclusive lattices

accepted.question_text: Determine whether there is an algorithm that decides, for a given finite set of finite semigroups, whether the inclusive variety it generates can be defined by a finite system of elementary identical inclusions, or prove that no such algorithm exists.
accepted.context_brief: finite basis problem for inclusive varieties

evidence.quote:

accepted.question_text: Determine (i) classes of semigroups in which elementary inclusive varieties form a sublattice of the lattice of inclusive varieties and (ii) nonelementary inclusive varieties that form an upper subsemilattice inside the lattice of inclusive varieties of periodic semigroups.

evidence.quote:
Problem 6.11. (G. Mashevitzky)
(1) Describe classes of semigroups in which elementary inclusive varieties form a sublattice of
the lattice of inclusive varieties.
(2) Describe nonelementary inclusive varieties that form an upper subsemilattice in the lattice
of inclusive varieties within the class of periodic semigroups.

accepted.question_text: Characterize (i) pargoids of projections, meaning idempotents in the semigroup of all transformations, (ii) pargoids of matrix units, and (iii) pargoids of idempotents arising from the basic classes of semigroups.

evidence.quote:
Problem 7.1. (E.S. Lyapin)
(1) Characterize pargoids of projections (idempotents in the semigroup of all transformations).
(2) Characterize the pargoids of matrix units.
(3) Characterize the pargoids of idempotents of the basic classes of semigroups.

accepted.question_text: For the main classes of mathematical structures and their natural pargoids of transformations, determine which classes of structures are determined up to isomorphism by those pargoids, and find pargoids of transformations that are themselves determined up to isomorphism by their endomorphism semigroup or automorphism group.

evidence.quote:

(1) For the main classes of mathematical structures and natural pargoids of transformations,
determine the classes of structures that are defined by these pargoids up to isomorphism.
(2) Find pargoids of transformations that are determined up to isomorphism by their semigroup
of endomorphisms (or group of automorphisms).

accepted.question_text: Characterize pargoids of transformations that admit an internal semigroup extension.

evidence.quote:
Problem 7.3. (E.S. Lyapin) Characterize pargoids of transformations that admit an internal

accepted.question_text: Classify the varieties of involuted semigroups for which the quasivarieties of relational models representable in those varieties are finitely axiomatizable.
